wps.title: Lesson format version, strict scene schemas, cheaper library import
wps.brief:
Close the rest of Q-04 and D-06 (wave A already validates tutor checkpoints and runs the lesson-locale check in the image build). Read both register entries and .claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/lesson-engine.md first.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (a) `formatVersion: 1` becomes required on every lesson file: lessonFileSchema gets `formatVersion: z.literal(1)`; a one-off script (portal/scripts/add-format-version.ts, kept, idempotent) adds the field as the FIRST key of every file under portal/content/library/lessons (106 English + 954 translations) preserving each file's formatting and key order otherwise; the Studio writers (src/server/ai-verify.ts, the lesson schema in src/server/actions/secops.ts) write formatVersion 1; the i18n/translation scripts under portal/scripts that write lesson files carry it over. (b) Pin the `stage` shape of tutor beats in validate.ts from what the 1,060 files actually contain (survey them in the script first) and remove `passthrough()` scene by scene only where the typecheck and the content test stay green; leave a passthrough where a key the player reads is not in the schema and list those in the summary. (c) D-06: the library upsert in src/server/services/library.ts updates a row only when its content changed (`where scenes is distinct from excluded.scenes`, same for titles), bootstrap logs the import duration and the number of rows written; no skip-and-alert (a bad file must still fail, as ADR-034's policy says). Run tests/content.test.ts, the lesson-locale checker (`npx tsx scripts/check-lesson-locales.ts --coverage`: all 954 translations must still pass) and the Studio tests.
acceptance: Every lesson file carries formatVersion 1 and a file without it fails validation (test); the 954 translations still pass the checker
Studio-written lessons validate; passthrough removed where safe (summary lists the rest)
Library import writes only changed rows and logs its duration (test); typecheck, lint, content and Studio tests pass

wps.title: Background jobs and risk recomputation at scale, tenant-scoped lookups
wps.brief:
Close D-03 and D-10. Read both register entries first (D-03's smallest fix is the design).
DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) recomputeRisk writes scores in one statement per chunk of 500 (`update users set risk_score = v.score from (values …) as v(id, score) where users.id = v.id::uuid`, PGlite-compatible); (2) a `job_runs` ledger (job text, tenant_id uuid, ran_at timestamptz, primary key (job, tenant_id); schema.ts only, no committed migration) gates reminders, manager alerts and refreshers to once per hour per organisation; dailySnapshot and scheduledReports keep their day gate; an overrunning tick never skips an hour; (3) launchCampaign inserts recipients and outbox rows in chunks of 500 through a new array variant queueEmails(db, tenantId, mails[], { defer: true }) in mail.ts (queueEmail stays and delegates); (4) workspace.ts recomputes only the affected people after an assignment change (diff of resolveAssignments before/after), or defers a whole-tenant recompute to the next tick when more than 2,000 active people are affected; (5) D-10: a `tenantModules(v)` predicate exported from queries/catalog.ts and used in queries/admin.ts and actions/people.ts so no lookup reads another organisation's modules or lessons; (6) portal/load/launch.js: a k6 script (not run here) with the scenario from the register and a README line. Tests: batched recompute equals the old per-row result on 1,200 seeded people; hourly gate (two ticks within an hour run once, a tick after an hour runs again, an overrun does not skip); chunked launch creates every recipient and mail; affected-only recompute; tenant-scoped lookups (risk-league and learner-queries tests stay green).
acceptance: Risk recompute is one UPDATE per 500 people and matches the old result (test)
Per-organisation hourly gating with the job_runs ledger (tests for once/again/overrun)
Campaign launch inserts in chunks; assignment changes recompute only affected people (tests)
Module and lesson lookups are organisation-scoped (tests); typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

wps.title: Per-route message bundles, lazy mascot engine, avatar route
wps.brief:
Close D-04 (all three pieces) and Q-02 (a)(b). Read both register entries first. D-09 (deleting the Rive assets) is an owner decision: do not delete anything.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) Messages: the root layout provides only the namespaces every surface needs (survey `useTranslations("` per route group first and list the namespaces per group in your summary); each route-group layout under src/app/(learner|admin|secops|public …) wraps its tree in its own NextIntlClientProvider with `pick(messages, [its namespaces])` plus an AzNumbersGate; a test renders each group's provider with its pick and greps the group's client components for cross-namespace use so a MISSING_MESSAGE cannot reach production. (2) Mascot: cat-mascot.tsx imports the engine's types only and loads createCat/mascotAutoWeights with a dynamic import inside the effect that creates the instance; scroll-cat/home-mascot already tolerate a late instance; eslint.config.mjs comment corrected to match README (engine.js is the source). (3) Avatars: route handler src/app/api/avatar/[userId]/route.ts answers the stored data URL's bytes for the viewer's own organisation only (cache-control private, max-age 3600, 404 otherwise); the viewer and the people page carry `/api/avatar/<id>` (or null) instead of base64; the session select lists user columns without avatarUrl; grep every avatarUrl reader (header, profile, exports) and adapt. Verify in your summary the first-load transfer of /sign-in and /app before and after (next build output or a measured HTML size) — numbers, not adjectives. Tests: avatar route tenant scope and cache header; provider pick test; mascot test file stays green.
acceptance: Each route group ships only its namespaces (test) and no client component reads a namespace its group does not provide (test)
The mascot engine is not in the first-load bundle of /sign-in (build output cited in the summary)
Avatars are served by a tenant-scoped route with private caching (test); no base64 avatar in the session or page payloads
typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; browser-visible behaviour unchanged (summary names what to check after the merge)

wps.title: One action result shape, a client helper with toast and retry, segment error boundaries
wps.brief:
Close the client half of Q-03 (plan item 3.4). Read the Q-03 register entry first and survey every `useTransition` call site under portal/src (36 at the time of the register).
DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) src/lib/action-result.ts exports `ActionResult<T> = { ok: true } & T | { ok: false; error: string }` and small helpers; server actions that already return this shape are typed with it (no behaviour change). (2) src/components/ui/use-action.ts: `useAction(action, { onSuccess, successToast?, errorMap? })` wrapping useTransition + the existing toast, mapping known error keys to translated messages (common namespace), a generic translated failure for the rest, and a retry affordance on the toast for failures that are not validation errors. (3) error.tsx for the learner, admin and super segments (and the public segment if it lacks one) using the existing RetryButton, ten-locale strings in the common namespace, logging through the server log where applicable. (4) Migrate the useTransition call sites to useAction EXCEPT these files, which other packages of this wave own and which you must not touch: portal/src/components/player/*, portal/src/app/(admin)/admin/campaigns/new/*, portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx, portal/src/components/admin/studio-*.tsx, portal/src/components/admin/person-actions.tsx, people-client.tsx, platform-client.tsx; list the skipped sites in your summary for a follow-up. Keep every validation message exactly as it is shown today. Tests: the helper (success, mapped error, unmapped error, retry) and one migrated dialog rendering its error state; the i18n parity test.
acceptance: useAction helper exists with tests; migrated call sites show translated errors with retry; no behaviour change for valid input
Segment error boundaries exist in ten locales
Files owned by other packages untouched (summary lists skipped sites); typecheck, lint, touched tests pass

wps.title: Stable scene environment, scene render tests, server-side template preview, texts out of code

DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) player.tsx builds `env` once with useMemo on its real inputs and wraps the callbacks in useEffectEvent so its identity is stable; then the suppressed effect dependencies in scenes.tsx that only hid `env` are restored and the suppressions deleted; verify narration does not double-fire on an env change (summary explains how you checked). wps.title: Read-only reporting API with scoped tokens
wps.brief:
Close M-07 (A) (plan item 3.7, the API-key half). Read the M-07 register entry first and src/server/auth/api.ts, src/server/auth/permissions.ts, the report routes under src/app/api/admin/reports and people, and the sessions table pattern in schema.ts.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) Table api_tokens (schema.ts only, no committed migration): id = sha256 of the token, tenant_id, name, permissions (jsonb list restricted to read permissions: reports.read, people.read, audit.read), created_by, created_at, last_used_at, revoked_at. (2) Minting: a tenant administrator creates a token in Settings → Integrations (name + permission checkboxes), sees the secret exactly once (the UI shows it in a copy field and never again), can revoke; audit 'api_token.created' / 'api_token.revoked'; at most 20 active tokens per organisation. (3) apiViewer accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>`: resolves the hash, refuses revoked tokens, builds a Viewer limited to the token's permissions (never a session user), updates last_used_at (throttled), rate-limits per token (the existing helper), and audits refusals. The existing routes /api/admin/reports/[kind] (csv|xlsx) and /api/admin/people/[kind] then serve machine clients unchanged; no write route accepts a token. (4) docs/API.md: a 'Reporting API' section (auth header, permissions, rate limit, examples with curl, error codes). (5) Tests: token mint/revoke/limit, bearer access to a report, refusal of a revoked token, of a write route, of another organisation's report, per-token rate limit, audit rows. Ten-locale strings.
acceptance: Tokens are minted once-visible, scoped, revocable, limited per organisation, audited (tests)
Bearer access serves the report routes with the token's permissions only; write routes and other organisations refuse (tests)
docs/API.md documents the reporting API; ten-locale strings with parity; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass; nothing under portal/drizzle committed

wps.title: Inbound report address: forwarded suspicious mail becomes a threat report
wps.brief:
Close M-06 (plan item 3.7, the reporting-channel half). Read the M-06 register entry and src/server/services/threats.ts (submitThreatReport, token matching), src/server/actions/security.ts and the Settings → Integrations card first.
DECISIONS TAKEN: (1) POST /api/inbound/[tenant] authenticated by a per-organisation inbound secret (TenantSettings.integrations.inboundSecret, generated in Settings → Integrations with a 'regenerate' button and a copy field; shown once) sent as a bearer header; body: the provider's parsed message as JSON { from, to, subject, text, html? } (document the generic shape; Mailgun/SES/Postmark adapters are the owner's provider choice — one 'generic JSON' adapter now). (2) The reporter is the active person of that organisation whose e-mail equals `from` (case-insensitive); unknown senders are refused with 202 (no information leak, no XP); the first /t/<token> link in the text is passed as url so threats.ts matches the simulation; details capped at 4,000 characters; rate limit per organisation; audit 'threat.reported' as the UI path does; recomputeRisk when the report matched a simulation. (3) Learner hint in the security.report namespace: 'forward the mail to <address>' shown only when the organisation configured the address (TenantSettings.integrations.inboundAddress, free text set by the administrator). (4) docs/API.md section 'Inbound report address'. Tests in tests/secops-flows.test.ts: a forwarded simulation mail files a matched report, an unknown sender is ignored, a wrong secret is refused, rate limit.
acceptance: A forwarded simulation mail becomes a matched threat report for the right person; unknown senders, wrong secrets and floods are refused (tests)
Administrators configure the secret and the address in Settings → Integrations; learners see the hint when configured (ten locales)
docs/API.md documents the endpoint; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass

wps.title: Dependency currency, legal text corrections, flaky tests and review nits from wave A
wps.brief:
Close D-07 (what wave A left), SEC 'not verified' items (plan 3.12) and the nits the wave A reviewers left open. Read the D-07 register entry and docs/build/OPEN-QUESTIONS.md item 26 (the lawyer's list) first.
(1) D-07: the three workflows under .github/workflows use `node-version-file: portal/.nvmrc`; verify every Dependabot option in .github/dependabot.yml against the GitHub docs (fetch them) and fix what is invalid; document in docs/OPERATIONS.md what the first gitleaks history run will report (the allowlisted historical commits) and the weekly cadence; run `npm outdated` in portal and put the list with the major updates to schedule (including the @anthropic-ai/sdk 1.x migration and its four call sites) into your summary for OPEN-QUESTIONS — do not install anything. (2) Legal corrections in all ten languages (by meaning, glossaries in .claude/skills/cyclowareness-experience/references/glossaries/, placeholders untouched): privacy §9 must describe the isolation that exists (per-organisation checks in every server action and route, an automated cross-tenant test suite) and not claim row-level security; the AI Sel retention row says tutor answers are kept up to 12 months (the clean-up job deletes them after 365 days); the §6.2 sentence about platform mail must match the code (read OPEN-QUESTIONS item 26 for the exact discrepancy); LDAP mentions removed where the offer no longer lists it. List every changed sentence per language in your summary for the lawyer. (3) Flaky or boundary-sensitive tests: the TOTP replay test must not depend on the 30-second step boundary (fix the clock in the test), the drill-service 'no person left' guard and the auth-security timing tests must pass 10 runs in a row (`npx vitest run <file> --repeat 10` or a loop) — fix the test or the code, never by widening timeouts alone. (4) The wave A change-password form shows each rule error on the field it belongs to and ties it with aria-describedby (profile security). (5) SEC I-3: document in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md why the CSP keeps 'unsafe-inline' for styles (Tailwind runtime) and what would be needed to drop it. (6) Link fallback, found in the wave B browser pass: after a reset or invite link is created in portal/src/components/admin/people-client.tsx (about line 164) and portal/src/components/admin/person-actions.tsx (about line 81), a failed clipboard write falls back to window.prompt. In embedded and sandboxed browsers that call throws, the link is lost and a new one needs the password again. Never call window.prompt: keep the dialog open and show the link in a read-only field with a copy button and a status line for screen readers; strings in all ten locales (az en ru tr ro ka uk de fr ar); a test that makes the clipboard write fail and asserts the link is still shown. C3 also edits people-client.tsx, so keep the change local to the link handler.
acceptance: Workflows use the .nvmrc; Dependabot config valid per the GitHub docs (summary cites the pages)
Legal texts corrected in ten languages, placeholders untouched, legal/landing tests pass; change list per language in the summary
The named tests pass ten consecutive runs (summary shows the command and result); change-password errors are accessible
npm outdated list and the SDK migration plan in the summary; typecheck, lint, touched tests pass

wps.title: Key ring and retention follow-ups from the wave B review
wps.brief: Defensive hardening of two controls that wave B added; the open notes are in the result paragraphs of ADR-045 and ADR-048 in docs/build/DECISIONS.md. Read them first and do not edit DECISIONS, PROGRESS or OPEN-QUESTIONS (put ADR text in your summary). If the security audit already closed a point on your base commit, verify it with a test and say so instead of changing it again. (1) Key ring (portal/src/server/crypto.ts, portal/src/server/services/secret-rotation.ts, portal/scripts/rotate-secret.ts, portal/src/server/env.ts): the key id is a plain sha256 of the secret with no purpose label. Nothing is deployed yet, so this is the moment to decide: either derive the id with a purpose label and update every fixture and test that pins v2 values, or keep it and record why it is safe. tests/env.test.ts has no cases for APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET: add them (blank, too short, equal to APP_SECRET, production without APP_SECRET). The rotation aborts when an organisation is deleted after the id list was read: skip the missing row, finish the others and report the skipped id. Add an npm script name for the rotation next to db:migrate in portal/package.json and use it in docs/OPERATIONS.md. (2) Retention (portal/src/server/jobs.ts about lines 395-410, portal/src/server/actions/settings.ts retentionSchema, portal/src/components/admin/settings-tabs.tsx, portal/src/lib/tenant-defaults.ts): auditMonths has no floor, so an administrator can choose one month and the audit trail, including the entry about that change, is erased a month later. Set a floor for the audit trail (0 still means keep everything; choose the floor from the legal texts in portal/content/legal and state it in the summary), refuse lower values on the server and explain the floor in the field hint. An emptied field is stored as 0, which silently means keep everything: reject an empty value with a field error. The cut-off uses setUTCMonth, which drifts up to three days at month end: clamp to the last day of the target month and test 31 March, 31 May and 29 February. Strings in all ten locales (az en ru tr ro ka uk de fr ar). No schema change, nothing under portal/drizzle.
acceptance: The key id decision is implemented or recorded with its reasoning; tests/crypto.test.ts and tests/auth-security.test.ts pass with the final derivation.
tests/env.test.ts covers APP_SECRET_PREVIOUS and APP_DOMAIN_PROOF_SECRET; a rotation with an organisation deleted mid-run completes and reports the skipped id, covered by a test.

The server refuses an audit retention below the floor and an empty retention field; the month cut-off is exact at month ends; tests/retention-settings.test.ts and tests/jobs-ops.test.ts cover each case.
Typecheck, lint and the touched tests pass.
